question: Which is the outermost layer of the earth composed of crust and upper mantle?
solution:
The correct answer is __the lithosphere__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The lithosphere is the solid, outer part of the Earth.
 
• It is an irregular surface with various landforms such as mountains, plateaus, deserts, plains, valleys, etc.
 
• It includes the brittle upper portion of the mantle and the crust.
 
• It is bounded by the atmosphere above and the asthenosphere below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The mesosphere is the 3rd layer of Earth's atmosphere.

 
 
• It extends from about 50 to 85 km above our planet.
 
• The mesosphere burns up most meteors and asteroids before they are able to reach the earth's surface.
 
 
 
• The stratosphere is the 2nd layer of Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
• It extends around 6 to 20 km above the Earth's surface.
 
• This is where you'll find the very important ozone layer which helps protect us from ultraviolet radiation (UV) from the sun.
 
 
 
• The asthenosphere is the mechanically weak and ductile region of the upper mantle of Earth.
 
 
• It lies below the lithosphere, between approximately 80 and 200 km below the surface, and extends as deep as 700 km.
 
• It enables the tectonic plates to move because the material under them can flow.
